**Disaster-liquidity checkpoint — 2026-09-20:** the NBER small-business
disaster-loan study is now promoted into Reader Finding #279. It supplies a
causal firm-level recovery stage—lower exit/bankruptcy and higher employment,
revenue, and private credit—while keeping worker quality, customer service,
owner-household recovery, and local meaning/action open.

**Eligibility-distribution checkpoint — 2026-09-20:** the NBER small-business
size-rule study is now promoted into Reader Finding #280. It adds a
policy-to-market-allocation mechanism: expanding eligibility toward larger
firms can redirect contracts and worsen revenue, exits, wages, and patenting
for affected smaller firms. The abstract-level evidence does not establish
customer welfare, worker security, or a universal policy effect.

The [material-time-household rotation screen](projects/us-household-constraint-cascade/material-time-household-rotation-screen-v1.md)
has now been completed. It confirms that the retained SIPP, SHED, MEPS, and
HRSA routes cover different pieces of the pressure-to-adaptation chain but do
not add a new same-unit remedy or durable-outcome stage. No new reader heading
is promoted from this screen. The next meaningful depth move remains an
authorized MEPS restaging or a user/account-holder supplied UAS file under
terms that expressly permit the workflow.

The [platform-choice finding](findings/us-platform-owned-products-matched-evidence-001.md)
completes the next consumer/platform/work-power pass. It adds a distinct
vertical-integration mechanism: short-run customer benefit can coexist with
long-run seller-access and choice-set questions. The next platform test remains
product/category persistence and seller entry/exit, not another ad-fee or
platform-use cross-tab.

The promotion rule for this rotation is strict: add a reader finding only if
the candidate contributes a new unit, mechanism, or stage. Existing SIPP,
SHED, ATUS, NHTS, MEPS, migration, and place layers already cover many
aggregate exposure patterns, so a duplicate cross-tab should become a matrix
or acquisition note instead. The preferred new stage is a dated household or
place episode with an alternative or non-use decision and a later bill,
work/care, service, movement, or recovery consequence. If the available
records stop at exposure or adaptation, record that boundary and rotate again.

The reader now contains 355 bounded findings across the 14-theme map. The last
rotation added social reciprocity, remedy reachability, local care usability,
marketplace visibility costs, household adaptation currencies, AI
capability/dependence, the smartphone attention/self-regulation split,
airport-transit usability, and geopolitical legitimacy across domestic and
foreign audiences.
The latest cultural-meaning addition separates broad approval of diversity from
agreement about company action and fairness, adding a workplace-legitimacy
bridge without claiming an observed organizational outcome.
The public-life engagement layer adds a civic-action counterexample: political
interest, news trust, community participation, and federal-government trust
form different combinations rather than one engagement ladder.
The press-freedom layer adds an information-legitimacy tension: press freedom
can be widely valued while limits for accuracy or security are also accepted,
with disagreement over who should hold corrective power.
The newest identity layer adds the belonging/treatment tension: Hispanic
identity can be highly central and socially connective while also being
reported as a barrier or site of unfair treatment.
The working-class identity layer adds a status boundary: self-described class
crosses income, education, and occupation. The political-typology layer adds a
coalition boundary: party labels contain cross-pressured groups with different
economic, cultural, institutional, and geopolitical views.
The current breadth audit found that the remaining recent candidates are
already represented through existing reader sections or cross-theme syntheses,
including the child-care eligibility-to-usable-care route and the labor/price/
income macro surfaces. Do not create another heading unless a candidate adds a
new unit, mechanism, or stage. The next serious move is therefore a lawful
same-unit/depth acquisition or follow-up, not another aggregate refresh.
While the account-controlled PSID/UAS/HRS routes remain unavailable, the
retained MEPS event spine is the active fallback depth route. Finding #214
records its exact boundary: month-ordered person/event scaffolding exists, but
event-specific alternatives, household choice, verified remedy, and recovery
do not. The next MEPS pass should test only fields that can be tied to that
same event and should stop when it reaches round-level context rather than
claiming an episode outcome.
The MEPS staging audit also records a crash-retention boundary: the historical
18,457-row JSONL and its source files under `/tmp/cgtm-meps-2024` are no longer
present. The committed stage-coverage output and hash preserve the prior
bounded result, but no rerun or extension should be claimed until the approved
MEPS source files are restored.
**Workspace recheck — 2026-09-21:** the four expected local acquisition
locations (`/tmp/cgtm-meps-2024`, `/tmp/us-broad-sipp-2025`,
`/tmp/us-broad-psid`, and `/tmp/cgtm-uas`) remain absent. The repository still
contains documentation, field audits, scripts, and bounded public comparators,
not the respondent directories themselves. This confirms that the next valid
depth move is either an authorized file handoff or another public record that
adds a later receipt, operating, durability, or response stage; it does not
authorize a synthetic household sequence or a re-run through restricted data.
**Public deepening scan — 2026-09-21:** current official material was checked
for a later infrastructure or geopolitical stage. FERC's large-load docket
still describes an advance notice of proposed rulemaking and public-input
stage, while its June orders direct regional operators to justify or reform
tariffs; neither source supplies a named facility's final compliance, bill,
reliability, or household result. NATO's CWIX 2026 report describes more than
600 capabilities and 30,000 interoperability tests, and NATO's public-private
resilience guidance calls for planning and coordination, but neither supplies
mission-level external response, public consent, or durable civilian-service
effect. These are useful boundary updates, not new end-to-end endpoints. The
next valid move remains a named project, account, capability, or affected unit
followed into receipt, operation, burden, acceptance, response, durability, or
exit. A September 15 PJM education session and redlined proposed ride-through
language add a more specific standards-design stage, while PJM's planned
November filing remains future action; neither establishes adopted requirements,
facility compliance, household bills, outages, or local acceptance.

**Institution-specific confidence checkpoint — 2026-09-21:** Gallup's June
2026 survey adds a distinct legitimacy map: average confidence remains low,
but small business is rated much more favorably than large technology
companies, and the largest partisan gap is attached to the presidency. This
does not show performance, dependence, switching, or withdrawal. The next
valid test is an institution-specific encounter followed through response,
continued use, complaint, switching, or political action.

**Information-verification checkpoint — 2026-09-21:** AP-NORC's *State of the
Facts* survey adds a new information-legitimacy stage. Trust in federal
information fell across major topics, while many adults reported difficulty
checking candidate claims and low confidence in AI-generated information. This
is a cross-sectional trust and perceived-verification-cost finding, not an
accuracy audit or a measured path to persuasion, correction, voting, or
withdrawal. The next test is a lawful information episode preserving source,
search effort, verification, correction, confidence, and later action.

**Local-reciprocity checkpoint — 2026-09-21:** Pew's neighborhood survey adds
**Local-national civic-capacity checkpoint — 2026-09-21:** the Trust for Civic
Life survey adds a selected rural counterexample: local trust, agency, and

also links agency to meaningful responsibility in problem-solving groups more
than to volunteer hours alone. Because recruitment ran through Civic Hub

difference contact, and later continuation or exit.

**Principle-versus-threat checkpoint — 2026-09-21:** AP-NORC's America 250
survey adds a national-identity counterexample: rights can be widely valued
while their safety is contested, and the American Dream can remain culturally
central while being judged unrealized. Party, age, and symbolic-display
differences are descriptive, not causal. The next test is a dated rights,
economic, or civic episode followed through interpretation and action.

**Coalition-configuration checkpoint — 2026-09-21:** Pew's 2026 typology adds
a nine-group map beneath the two-party surface. Within-party differences in
culture, material stress, political attention, alliance preferences, and views
of power are substantial. The groups are cluster-derived and descriptive, not
causal or permanent identities. The next test is a validated respondent or
dated episode that follows a cross-pressured group through information,
attribution, participation, switching, or non-use.

**Democracy-performance checkpoint — 2026-09-22:** Pew adds a distinct
evaluation layer: many Americans say the U.S. used to be a good democratic
example but is not now, and dissatisfaction is high but sharply partisan. The
survey does not identify reform preference, feasibility, turnout, protest, or
withdrawal. The next test is a dated institutional episode followed through
democratic judgment, reform demand, participation, and later action.

**Reform-feasibility checkpoint — 2026-09-22:** Pew's July analysis adds the
missing distinction between wanting change and believing change is achievable:
77% said major or complete reform is needed, while 27% were confident that
major change could happen. Roughly half were described as "pessimistic
reformers." Separate surveys also show majority support for several specific
reforms, but those answers are not one coordinated program. This is a public
attitude pattern, not evidence of action or successful reform; the next valid
test remains a dated institutional episode with reform preference, organizing,
institutional response, and later continuation or exit.

**Civic-reach/time checkpoint — 2026-09-22:** the Census/AmeriCorps 2023 civic
supplement is now promoted into the canonical registry. Formal volunteering
and informal neighbor help rose after the pandemic low, while mean and median
hours per formal volunteer fell. This is a reach-versus-time pattern, not a
measure of civic efficacy, organizational continuity, local repair, or later
political action. The next test is a place-linked or repeated civic record
that joins activity to time, transport, care, organizational response, and
continuation or exit.

**Smartphone self-regulation checkpoint — 2026-09-22:** Pew adds a personal
attention/control stage to the low-density platform lane. Many adults report
that smartphones help them stay informed and connected while also saying they
spend too much time on them; among those who tried to cut back, only a quarter
report being highly successful. This is not a device-log, addiction, health,
or durable-exit finding. The next test is a privacy-protected diary or device
record joining the target behavior to the reason for reduction, substitutes,
work/care constraints, and later continuation or exit.

**Airspace-response persistence checkpoint — 2026-09-22:** a NATO August 2026
account adds a repeated-incident response stage after airspace violations and
drone incidents affecting Poland and Romania. Solidarity, public attribution,
condemnation, and defensive reinforcement are visible; deterrence, changed
Russian behavior, host burden, and public acceptance remain open. The next
test is a dated incident-response ledger with independent verification,
duration, local effects, and later external behavior.

**Drinking-water infrastructure checkpoint — 2026-09-22:** EPA and CDC add an
essential-service and governance comparison. Community-water coverage is broad,
but private-well users carry more testing and maintenance responsibility while
EPA estimates a large lead-service-line replacement need. This is not a
household exposure, replacement, bill, health, or safe-service result. The next
test is a place-level water-system or private-well episode with notice, testing,
replacement or treatment, cost, outage, and later service or health outcome.

**Local-reciprocity checkpoint — 2026-09-21:** Pew's neighborhood survey adds
a cultural-support distinction that was not explicit in the main readout:
local trust and willingness to help can exceed people's expectation that help
will actually be available. This is a useful informal-capacity signal, not a
delivered-aid, burden, adequacy, or household-security finding. The next valid
test is a place-linked or repeated episode that observes help requested, help
delivered, helper cost, recipient result, and later continuity.
The geopolitical scan found a watch candidate in the Joint Expeditionary Force's
March 2026 statement: leaders describe progress in the JEF/Ukraine Enhanced
Partnership, future Ukrainian participation in JEF LION exercises, and aligned
response options. This adds a planned partner-integration route, not observed
partner behavior, public consent, deterrence, refusal, or changed external
conduct. Recheck after the exercise or a dated incident response.
**JEF follow-up scan — 2026-09-21:** later official JEF accounts now add a
real operating stage: a multinational escort rehearsal moved Danish military
equipment through the Baltic to Latvia, and a later exercise deployed a JEF
forward headquarters in northern Norway with host-nation support and NATO
coordination. This upgrades the candidate from planned integration to reported
cross-border operation, but it still does not show a real crisis response,
adversary change, local acceptance, community burden, or durable deterrence.
The Ukrainian-participation route remains a separate implementation watch item;
the records reviewed here do not show what Ukrainian units did or whether the
partnership changed another actor's behavior. See the [JEF operating
record](records/us-jef-lion-protector-baltic-express-2026.json), the [JEF
leaders' statement](https://jefnations.org/2026/03/30/joint-statement-from-the-leaders-of-the-joint-expeditionary-force-26-march-2026),
and the [UK-Ukraine declaration](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-ukraine-joint-statement-enhanced-security-and-defence-industrial-collaboration-declaration).
**Worker-remedy freshness check — 2026-09-21:** the Department of Labor's
FY2025 release reports more than $259 million in recovered back wages for
nearly 177,000 employees, while the current Workers Owed Wages route still
requires search, identity verification, a signed claim, supporting documents,
and electronic payment. The scale figure strengthens the institutional-recovery
stage but does not add worker-level receipt, adequacy, household relief, later
work, trust, or exit. Keep it as a public comparator, not a recovery rate or a
new end-to-end episode.
The CHIPS governance layer adds an industrial-capacity boundary: awards and
disbursements can advance while qualified output, workforce retention,
customer supply, governance alignment, and reduced foreign dependence remain
open.
The AI capability layer adds the adjacent adopt/adapt/advance boundary: access
to imported tools can be useful before local language fit, institutional
supervision, portability, or provider replaceability are established. Keep
capability, dependence, and geopolitical leverage as separate stages.
The international-legitimacy layer adds the external-reception boundary:
foreign publics, U.S. partisans, and U.S. institutions can interpret the same
material power differently. A shared description of interference does not
prove shared legitimacy, alliance trust, or changed external behavior.
The European Parliament Research Service's February 2026 transatlantic brief
adds analyst-level context on uncertainty about U.S. reliability across NATO,
Ukraine, trade, technology, climate, and China, while retaining shared
security and resilience interests as possible cooperation channels. It is not
a country-public survey or an observed alliance response; use it to define
candidate event windows and response fields, not to promote a legitimacy or
leverage claim. The new [event-country-party-year acquisition manifest](projects/ai-work-control/event-country-party-year-acquisition-manifest-v1.md)
turns that open bridge into a bounded candidate inventory, with Poland F-35,
JASSM-ER, Virginia large-load, and Pew audience records kept as separate
inputs until an observed external response is available.
The last item adds a consumer-culture example in which information and
connection utility coexist with perceived excess and mostly partial attempts
to cut back. These additions preserve breadth and sharpen the shared
conversion rule, but they do not close the portfolio's open middle.

The next pass should therefore prioritize one compact, lawful, same-unit or
same-organization episode with these fields:

```text
condition or shock
  -> attempted route and available alternative
  -> effort, time, money, and completion
  -> institutional or firm response
  -> actual receipt/use and adequacy
  -> later durability, trust, switching, non-use, or exit
```

Candidate lanes remain: a named worker remedy with payment and later work; a
recipient/account-level consumer or public-benefit correction; a property-level
insurance claim through repair and safe return; a care episode through usable
appointment and later health/work outcome; or a named infrastructure/defense
capability through delivery, acceptance, operation, replaceability, and an
affected actor's response. If the required authorized identifier or follow-up
is unavailable, record the acquisition boundary and do not promote another
aggregate result into an end-to-end claim.

**Atkins public-follow-up recheck — 2026-09-20:** searches of the Fair Work
Ombudsman route and broader public web results located the original 2016
underpayment/penalty record and the 2018 appeal-dismissal/payment record, but
no worker-specific later employment, adequacy, household, trust, recurrence,
or exit record for the ten named drivers. Current job postings associated with
the company are not evidence about those workers. Keep Atkins at
underpayment → enforcement → institutionally reported receipt, and treat the
later lived-recovery fields as an acquisition boundary ([2016 enforcement
record](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/newsroom/media-releases/2016-media-releases/july-2016/20160705-atkins-penalty);
[2018 payment follow-up](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/newsroom/media-releases/2018-media-releases/january-2018/20180117-atkins-appeal-dismissed)).

**Authenticated same-unit data gate — 2026-09-20:** a workspace inventory and
the current acquisition audits confirm that no PSID, UAS, or HRS respondent
file is locally retained. PSID public-use packages require researcher
registration and Conditions-of-Use acceptance; UAS downloads require
registration and its current terms restrict automated/LLM handling without
express authorization; HRS downloads require login. The executable next step
is therefore an authorized human-led handoff: obtain the smallest permitted
PSID Data Center extract or UAS Older Ages panel, then run the structural
identity, timing, weight, missingness, and overlap gates before estimating
anything. Until that authority and file state changes, keep the existing
public-data bridges as bounded context and do not manufacture a same-unit
end-to-end result from documentation alone.
The health-friction counterexample adds route specificity: prescription delay
and prior-authorization delay show different mixes of later perceived-health
change, so “institutional friction” is not one universal pathway.
The linked HTOPS bridge adds a material-to-political endpoint: expense
difficulty is followed by household pressure while institutional confidence
moves unevenly across the presidency, Congress, coercive institutions, and
statistical agencies.
The retail-activity comparison adds a consumer-firm boundary: nominal sales
can rise while real quantity, household room, firm margin, local access, and
customer welfare remain open.
The household-security baseline adds a national-clock boundary: high median
income can coexist with poverty, child poverty, and full-year uninsured status
without proving usable security for the same households.
The social-connection comparison adds a cultural boundary: communication can
remain comparatively stable while loneliness and support adequacy worsen, and
institutional confidence varies by the institution being judged.
The repeated-snapshot comparison adds a timing boundary: broad expense
pressure can look stable while food, energy, and institutional judgments move
on separate clocks; the snapshots are not a household panel.
The fraud/loss follow-up adds a consumer conversion rule: exposure, realized
loss, agency reporting, self-reported recovery, and restored security remain
separate, especially in the sparse recovery cell.
The interface synthesis adds the central conversion rule directly: formal
availability is not usable opportunity, and failed conversion costs are often
shifted into private time, money, disclosure, family help, non-use, or dependence.
These are
separate source universes, not one pooled result. They
strengthen the recurring conversion rule that formal capacity, practical use,
protected outcome, and durable belonging must be measured separately. The next
pass should seek a dated user or family episode with an alternative, effort,
completion, and later outcome—or rotate to another theme rather than add
another exposure-only cross-tab.

**Health-access gate checkpoint — 2026-09-19:** the new [Medicare Advantage
prior-authorization finding](projects/us-health-cost-household-choice/findings/us-health-cost-household-choice-014.md)
adds a current denial-to-appeal route. HHS OIG found 12% of SNF admission
requests denied across 19 plans; only 18% of denials were appealed, and 95% of
appealed denials were overturned. This strengthens the institutional-friction
middle without claiming that reversal produced timely admission, completed
rehabilitation, functional recovery, or trust. The next valid step remains a
request-level episode with delay, substitute care, out-of-pocket cost, and
later outcome.

**Medicare Advantage implementation-status recheck — 2026-09-29:** the [SNF
prior-authorization record](records/us-hhs-oig-medicare-snf-prior-authorization-2026.json)
was rechecked against the official HHS-OIG report page. All three CMS
recommendations remain marked open and unimplemented, with a tracker update
expected 2026-12-07. This updates the institutional-response stage only; it
does not add a beneficiary outcome, prove post-report plan behavior, or close
the route to admission timing, substitute care, recovery, household burden,
trust, or plan choice. The next decisive input remains an authorized
beneficiary or plan/provider episode.

**Benefit-control checkpoint — 2026-09-19:** the new [SNAP benefit-control
finding](projects/us-safety-net-access/findings/us-safety-net-access-019.md)
adds an important public-system failure stage: benefits can be formally issued
but become unusable when an EBT account is stolen. GAO reports more than $320
million in approved replacement benefits for nearly 679,000 households during
the covered statutory period, while warning that the data understate theft and
do not show individual replacement timing, food gaps, or durable recovery.
Recipient controls, card modernization, and monitoring are institutional
responses, not proof of restored food security. The next valid step remains a
privacy-approved same-episode route with theft, claim, replacement, interim
food/cash substitution, next-month stability, and later trust/reporting.

**Worker payment-verification checkpoint — 2026-09-19:** the worker lane now
separates two institutional states that must not be pooled. The Workers Owed
Wages route exposes recovered money that a worker still has to find, verify,
claim, and receive; the separate PAID program requires an employer to pay
within 15 days and provide WHD proof of payment. The second is stronger
administrative verification, but neither public route shows worker cashing,
adequacy, household recovery, durable work, trust, or exit. Keep both as
reachability counterpoints and target same-worker payment and later-outcome
fields rather than another aggregate recovery total.

**HTOPS denominator-integrity checkpoint — 2026-09-19:** the April-to-June
fraud follow-up memo now matches the machine record and linkage audit: 8,850
April rows, 7,485 June rows, and 6,564 exact `SCRAMID` links. This does not
change the estimates; it removes a stale denominator before the linked panel
is used in another synthesis.

The current material-exposure → political-meaning/action checkpoint is tracked
in the [focused status ledger](US-BROAD-MATERIAL-TO-ACTION-STATUS_V1.md). It
confirms that the program already has judgment, trust, action, turnout, and
panel-persistence surfaces; the next decisive addition is a dated event with
attribution, action route, response, and recovery—not another unaligned
sentiment cross-tab.

**Storage-aware selection decision (2026-09-16):** the local 2025 SIPP
`pu2025.csv` and `rw2025.csv` archives already support the current resource,
tenure, utility, work, care, food, and transition screens, including compatible
Fay–BRR reruns. The next SIPP contribution should therefore be a dated bill,
shutoff, assistance, or service episode—or the authenticated PSID family
design—not another adjacent cross-tab. This preserves storage and keeps the
program focused on closing an end-to-end arrow.

**Material/time recheck (2026-09-17):** the retained SIPP slice and existing
240-replicate reproduction audit were revalidated as the current evidence
base. The utility-to-following-work screen remains reproducible descriptive
context, but `ETIMELOST`/`ATIMELOST` are conditional fall child-care fields
and `EPAY`/`EPAYHELP` are care-payment/help fields; they do not supply a dated
utility bill or service event with a general monthly time-displacement
outcome. No redundant trend record is promoted. The next smallest aligned
acquisition is therefore one event-compatible bill, shutoff, payment-plan,
assistance, or service record with follow-up, or the authenticated PSID
2019/2021/2023 structural extract. Until then, keep the SIPP result bounded
as a monthly transition screen and leave recovery, alternatives, control,
meaning, and action open.

The Small Acts of Kindness/Ipsos record added a route from energy and food trade-offs through isolation, mediated companionship, printed information, material warmth and perceived care in a targeted support encounter. The next test is whether support changes energy use, food adequacy, benefits or advice take-up, health, service continuity and repeat connection; selected recipient feedback remains insufficient outcome or population evidence.

**Prior registry checkpoint (2026-09-28, cultural-institution rotation):** The trend registry held 1674 records and
4990 observations. The Ipsos–Independent Football Regulator record added a route from club heritage, place, ritual, community presence and fan engagement through distress, prospective collective action and formal heritage/voice regulation. The next test is whether fan consultation changes documented ownership, stadium, identity, ticket and financial decisions, and whether those changes preserve local access, club survival and durable trust; stated action remains insufficient evidence of realized influence.

**Prior registry checkpoint (2026-09-28, household-expectations rotation):** The trend registry held 1673 records and
4986 observations. The ECB Consumer Expectations Survey record added a route from income position through inflation perception, unemployment expectations, housing-price expectations, mortgage cost, credit access and household room. The next test is whether this expectation asymmetry becomes realized differences in housing access, borrowing, major-purchase delay, savings drawdown, employment exposure and political attribution; the monthly survey remains insufficient evidence of those downstream outcomes.

**Prior registry checkpoint (2026-09-28, wartime-legitimacy rotation):** The trend registry held 1672 records and
4982 observations. The KIIS Ukraine record added a route from expected winter energy attack through civilian endurance, regional exposure, leader trust, service experience, anti-corruption accountability, and national resistance. The next test is whether named energy-restoration, resilience, anti-corruption, civil-defense, or public-information interventions preserve service access, household recovery, public influence and durable legitimacy; the hypothetical wartime scenario remains insufficient observed-outcome evidence.

The preceding Equifax Market Pulse rotation adds a route from measured asset and payment capacity through a divergence between sentiment and financial position, and a paused-but-unequal K-shaped distribution. The next test is whether asset buffers predict who absorbs energy, food, medical, housing, repair, or job shocks, and whether sentiment predicts behavior after those buffers are measured; a proprietary aggregate index remains insufficient household outcome evidence.

The preceding STAATUS Index rotation adds a route from AAPI cultural visibility through contested Americanness, weak generalized recognition, geopolitical threat framing, race-based exposure, and transit/online unsafety. The next test is whether named school, transit, platform, cultural-program, local-business, or anti-harassment interventions produce observed participation, reporting, protection, institutional response, and repeat belonging; stated openness and cultural visibility remain insufficient outcome evidence.

The preceding UK Women in Research Charter rotation adds a route from near-parity at research entry through caring responsibilities, short contracts, time-intensive norms, biased assessment, and the formal-flexibility/enactment gap into senior-level attrition. The next test is whether signatory-level leave, care-cost, flexible-grant, promotion, recruitment, and safety data show usable reform and improved retention; a voluntary charter and policy commitment remain insufficient outcome evidence.

The preceding Afrobarometer East Africa reproductive-autonomy rotation adds a route from public support for women’s autonomy and sexuality education through marital and age gatekeeping, contraception, abortion circumstance, institutional delivery, and usable reproductive agency. The next test is whether named sexuality-education, contraceptive, maternal-health, or reproductive-rights interventions produce safe, confidential, affordable access and durable household bargaining power; stated autonomy remains insufficient proxy.

The preceding Young Futures Hubs interim evaluation remains an active youth-service implementation rotation: accessible youth spaces and trusted relationships connect warm handovers, targeted and specialist support, co-design, employability, belonging, safety, and measurement capacity. Its next test is whether named hub, referral, youth-council, mental-health, employability, or community-safety interventions produce unique sustained engagement, completed handoffs, verified outcomes, youth decision influence, and durable participation; reach and attendance remain insufficient proxies.

**Current registry checkpoint (2026-09-28, social-pressure rotation):** The trend registry now holds 1621 records and 4784 observations. The St Patrick's Irish mental-health and stigma publication adds the route from cost, housing, loneliness, climate concern, digital exposure, stigma, silence, and support-seeking into reachable care, discrimination reduction, and durable participation. The next tests are whether reported pressure predicts observed help-seeking, whether support remains reachable across housing and income strata, and whether reduced stigma becomes less silence and better service continuity rather than only a favorable attitude.

**Current registry checkpoint (2026-09-28, consumer-media rotation):** The trend registry now holds 1622 records and 4788 observations. The thinkTV/Ipsos Ad Nation publication adds the route from professional media assumptions through public platform use, advertising trust, AI-content concern, social-advertising credibility, shared television, and cultural attention. The next tests are whether correcting audience models changes channel choice, exposure quality, trust, and realized action across groups rather than merely changing industry narrative.

**Current registry checkpoint (2026-09-28, youth-cultural rotation):** The trend registry now holds 1623 records and 4792 observations. The Pacsun/GlobalData Youth Report adds the route from noisy public information through family/friend trust, high AI adoption but low consequential trust, delayed financial independence, parental reliance, and mental-health-centered future goals. The next tests are whether selective delegation is stable across age and household-resource groups, whether material dependence changes trust and aspiration, and whether AI use becomes capability or merely another layer of guided consumption.

**Current registry checkpoint (2026-09-28, AI-trust rotation):** The trend registry now holds 1624 records and 4796 observations. Gartner's consumer survey adds the route from synthetic content saturation through reduced influencer reliance, greater reliance on real people, lower brand trust, and pressure for transparent quality governance. The next tests are whether disclosure, human expertise, and quality controls restore source trust across consumer groups and whether “AI fatigue” changes behavior rather than only stated attitudes.

**Current registry checkpoint (2026-09-28, multilateral-legitimacy rotation):** The trend registry now holds 1625 records and 4800 observations. The UN Foundation/GeoPoll poll adds the route from global turbulence through UN necessity, delivery frustration, conflict-prevention priorities, outward-facing leadership, selection awareness, gendered representation, and North-South trust differences. The next tests are whether a leadership transition produces visible delivery, public attention, equitable voice, and renewed trust rather than only a favorable mandate.

**Current registry checkpoint (2026-09-28, local-consent rotation):** The trend registry now holds 1626 records and 4804 observations. The UMass Poll adds the route from national AI ambition through local environmental and resource concerns, utility costs, land use, community fit, cross-partisan opposition, and political accountability. The next tests are whether enforceable community benefits, rate protections, local participation, and transparent siting convert strategic necessity into consent rather than backlash.

**Current registry checkpoint (2026-09-28, diaspora-cultural rotation):** The trend registry now holds 1627 records and 4808 observations. The [Frontiers cultural-identity record](records/comparative-frontiers-ethnic-chinese-cultural-identity-southeast-asia-2026.json) adds the route from diaspora heritage identity through Chinese-content exposure, visits to China, language, media mediation, and national context across Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand. The next tests are whether content and contact produce durable cultural practice, whether pathways differ by generation and local institutions, and whether identity remains distinct from political allegiance or generalized pan-ethnic identity.

**Current registry checkpoint (2026-09-28, consumer-governance rotation):** The trend registry now holds 1628 records and 4812 observations. The [YouGov financial-services AI record](records/comparative-yougov-consumer-duty-ai-financial-services-2026-human-fallback-trust.json) adds the route from AI adoption through perceived cost/profit motives, reduced human interaction, vulnerable-customer exposure, human fallback, accountable decisions, and data protection. The next tests are whether named deployments preserve human escalation, explain decisions, provide remedy, and improve realized customer outcomes across older and vulnerable customers rather than only changing stated confidence.

**Current registry checkpoint (2026-09-28, work-and-family meaning rotation):** The trend registry now holds 1629 records and 4816 observations. The [YouGov values-of-children-and-work record](records/comparative-yougov-values-children-work-2026-success-time-meaning.json) adds the route from childrearing ideals through work-time preferences, remote-work legitimacy, passion-versus-pay, and age/ideology/education/parenthood differences. The next tests are whether named work, leave, childcare, or remote-work interventions make preferred autonomy, care time, security, and purpose materially reachable across groups rather than leaving them as stated ideals.

**Current registry checkpoint (2026-09-28, employment-continuity rotation):** The trend registry now holds 1631 records and 4824 observations. The [Carers UK work and unpaid-care record](records/comparative-carers-uk-work-unpaid-care-2026-employment-tipping-point.json) adds the route from unpaid care inside working life through reduced hours, stress, and employment exit. The next tests are whether care intensity, employer flexibility, formal-care access, and paid leave preserve employment continuity and reduce household income loss.

**Current registry checkpoint (2026-09-28, election-information rotation):** The trend registry now holds 1632 records and 4828 observations. The [Catawba College–YouGov Ballots & Bots record](records/comparative-catawba-yougov-election-ai-authenticity-trust-2026.json) adds the route from suspected synthetic political content through authenticity uncertainty, conditional election legitimacy, trusted local verification, and demand for disclosure and platform accountability. The next tests are whether provenance labels, rapid correction, and local election-office communication preserve acceptance of results.

**Current registry checkpoint (2026-09-28, local-consumer rotation):** The trend registry now holds 1633 records and 4832 observations. The [SOCi Local Discovery Index record](records/comparative-soci-local-discovery-ai-verification-loop-2026.json) adds the route from AI-mediated local discovery through cross-channel verification, review-based remedy, category-specific visibility, and unequal discovery access. The next tests are whether local consumers complete the verification loop, whether stale information causes measurable diversion or exclusion, and whether responsive reputation systems restore conversion.

**Current registry checkpoint (2026-09-28, education-legitimacy rotation):** The trend registry now holds 1634 records and 4836 observations. The [Public First cross-party education record](records/comparative-public-first-education-cross-party-technical-pathways-delivery-2026.json) adds the route from technical-pathway and adult-readiness preferences through cross-party policy agreement, implementation skepticism, local-capacity concerns, and transparent delivery. The next tests are whether technical routes produce actual enrollment, completion, work transitions, earnings, and durable trust rather than only broad stated support.

**Current registry checkpoint (2026-09-28, employer-transition rotation):** The trend registry now holds 1635 records and 4840 observations. The [WorldSkills UK/Public First Ready to Work record](records/comparative-worldskillsuk-public-first-ready-to-work-employer-skills-2026.json) adds the employer-side route from harder youth entry into work through employability-skill signaling, firm capability, structured demonstrations, and unequal access to credible early-career pathways. The next tests are whether competitions, work experience, and technical routes change interviews, offers, retention, earnings, and subgroup access.

**Current registry checkpoint (2026-09-28, home-resilience rotation):** The trend registry now holds 1636 records and 4844 observations. The [IKEA Life at Home 2026 record](records/comparative-ikea-life-at-home-2026-home-resilience-control-sustainability.json) adds the route from external uncertainty through home security, comfort, control, domestic agency, and savings/health-motivated climate action. The next tests are whether housing quality, energy cost, health, repair/reuse, and income-stratified access to household agency move together in observed behavior.

**Latest continuation:** The ONS Great Britain wellbeing/loneliness publication adds a repeated official-survey route through anxiety, loneliness, hope, cost-of-living and housing salience, and age-stratified cultural/geopolitical issue priorities. The next test is whether these reported states connect to actual household adaptation, service use, political action, and durable belonging.

### Health-cost legitimacy acquisition gate

The immediate health-cost pass now has two executable registration-gated
routes. The [UAS audit](projects/us-health-cost-household-choice/uas-health-cost-legitimacy-acquisition-audit-v1.md)
and its monthly follow-up scripts target a reported medical-expense shock or
an Older Ages monthly event followed by later health, work, pain,
life-satisfaction, or meaning outcomes, with UAS 537/698 supplying richer care,
satisfaction, and trust fields. The Older Ages panel is the narrower,
event-first route for adults 50+; the October 2023-present Monthly Panel is the
broader adult route. The [HRS audit](projects/us-health-cost-household-choice/hrs-health-cost-trust-acquisition-audit-v1.md)
provides an age-50-plus re-test using unaffordable-care reasons and trust in
Medicare/Medicaid and insurers. The first acquired-file gate is structural:
hashes, person keys, module overlap, eligibility, weights, timing, and
missingness. Only after that gate can a same-person health-cost-to-trust or
recovery result enter the atlas.

**HRS access recheck — 2026-09-18:** the legacy HRS public-data page now
redirects to the current HRS Data Downloads host, whose live page requires
login for file downloads. The [machine access recheck](projects/us-health-cost-household-choice/data/hrs-access-recheck-2026-09-18.json)
records the moved route and confirms that no HRS respondent file is locally
available. HRS remains a documented fallback, not an executable estimate, and
the first authorized pass must still run the structural merge audit.

**UAS Comprehensive Panel recheck — 2026-09-18:** USC now documents a June
2026 long-format Comprehensive Panel Dataset with one respondent-by-wave row,
quarterly updates, harmonized health/financial/employment/wellbeing content,
`uasid` linkage, and weights. Downloads remain registration-required, and no
respondent file is locally retained. This strengthens the acquisition design
but does not replace the narrower Older Ages event-first file or create an
estimate. The [machine recheck](projects/us-health-cost-household-choice/data/uas-access-recheck-2026-09-18.json)
records the current route, missingness/weight boundary, and stop conditions.
The current UAS terms also restrict automated access/extraction and LLM
management or analysis of CESR-distributed data without express written
authorization, so this remains an acquisition specification rather than an
authorized processing route.

The new [MEPS institutional-friction follow-up finding](projects/us-health-cost-household-choice/findings/us-health-cost-household-choice-011.md)
adds a bounded round-to-round screen while those acquisition gates remain open:
reported denial or prior-authorization delay is followed by more perceived
health worsening, but similar employment transitions. The result advances the
health-to-outcome arrow without closing claim timing, remedy, treatment
continuity, household adaptation, trust, or action.

The [program continuity ledger](US-BROAD-PROGRAM-CONTINUITY-LEDGER_V1.md) is
the durable long-term control record. This queue selects the next empirical
pass; it does not narrow or complete the program.

The reader-facing [source family map](../site/source-registry.html) now makes
the 114 recurring source families, their roles, evidence types, and
interpretation limits searchable. The financial-capacity review confirms that
the existing BEA, Federal Reserve, OFR, IMF FAS, World Bank Findex, SHED, and
New York Fed layers are complementary but not joinable into a new household
estimate without a shared person/account event key. The next pass therefore
must acquire or identify that dated event rather than restate provider,
macro, and survey aggregates as one causal story.

This queue is the handoff from the current evidence map to the next empirical
passes. Every pass must identify the unit, date, geography, denominator,
missingness, uncertainty, and arrow status. A source can deepen one arrow
without completing the societal chain.

## Active continuation checkpoint

The program has completed broad anchor passes across all 14 themes and has
recently added depth in four rotating lanes: household adaptation and care;
time, work, and life-stage distribution; local business and service capacity;
and migration, place, and infrastructure/state dependence. These passes are
cross-source comparisons and bounded same-respondent analyses where the data
permit. They do not yet establish a single population-wide causal chain.

The latest breadth rotations are the migration/place/belonging layer and the
consumer-culture/trust/status layer. The former is an explicit cross-source
comparison of new residents as workers, customers, neighbors, entrepreneurs,
and public-system users. The latter treats buying, searching, sharing,
reporting, help-seeking, switching, and staying as social and institutional
acts. Neither infers cultural meaning or political action from population
change, participation, trust, or service capacity; those require direct
resident/customer-level measures aligned to place, episode, and time.

The consumer lane now has a bounded cross-source synthesis that tests unequal
optionality under institutional mediation across confidence, payment systems,
platform civic attention, charitable-food access, and digital recourse. These
surfaces establish a research proposition and concrete missing fields; they do
not form a consumer welfare index or a same-customer causal chain.

The reader layer now has dedicated routes for material/time/care linkage,
political meaning across scales, AI use/work/contact/exit, public help and
judgment, housing/insurance/energy pressure, and consumer culture/trust/status.
These routes are presentation
artifacts built from the validated records; they do not add new estimates or
close the same-unit event arrows. The authenticated PSID package remains
absent. The 2025 SIPP archive, replicate-weight archive, and derived full-file
slice were historically held outside Git under `/tmp/us-broad-sipp-2025/`; a
current post-crash recheck finds that temporary directory absent. The
utility-to-following-work screen was previously rerun from that full slice and
reproduced its committed point estimates and intervals. A follow-on
utility/tenure/child-care comparison now supplies the compatible annual
`EWORKMORE` universe while preserving its mixed-clock boundary. The next SIPP
gate is therefore a dated bill/service event or the stronger authenticated
PSID acquisition, followed by explicit universe, retention, missingness,
weighting, and timing checks.

The plain-language care synthesis now makes unpaid eldercare explicit as
hidden social infrastructure: scale and care-day time are visible, while the
caregiver's displaced work, sleep, earnings, health, and household security
remain unmeasured in the public aggregate. This strengthens the societal
interpretation but does not change the next acquisition decision: the decisive
pass still needs a same-family care episode with a replacement option,
schedule/work response, recipient outcome, and later durability.

The local [utility-to-buffer transition gate](projects/us-household-calendar-integration/sipp-utility-buffer-following-gate-v1.md)
was then run against the same v18 slice and 240-replicate archive. Credit and
savings fields produced zero valid adjacent-month state changes, so they are
not an event-compatible monthly buffer trajectory in this public-use extract.
The next SIPP contribution must therefore use a dated bill, transaction,
shutoff, assistance, or service episode—or the authenticated PSID route—rather
than treating repeated account-status fields as borrowing, repayment, or
recovery.

The [canonical Al Hussein comparative remedy record](records/au-al-hussein-reactivation-deemed-work-2025.json)
adds a counterpattern to the Mansoor and Waheed stages: reactivation and
deemed work were ordered, and parties were directed to confer on lost pay, but
the checked public route contains no quantified payment order, receipt, actual
access, or later work/switching result. This advances procedural remedy
coverage without converting deemed work into wages or recovery.

The material/time/care pass has completed its local SIPP field-timing gate and
is preserved as an open acquisition route in the
[acquisition plan](projects/us-household-calendar-integration/material-time-care-linkage-acquisition-plan-v1.md)
and [PSID extract specification](projects/us-household-calendar-integration/psid-material-time-care-extract-spec-v1.md).
The practical-exit rotation has now completed its local observability audit,
including the [platform dry-run](projects/us-customer-automation-recourse/practical-exit-platform-ledger-dry-run-v1.md),
[CFPB dry-run](projects/us-customer-automation-recourse/cfpb-practical-exit-contract-dry-run-v1.md),

The capacity/dependence rotation has completed its local realization and

multi-disaster design. The retained result is abstract-level and does not
establish worker pay, customer prices/service continuity, owner-household
recovery, or local political meaning. The current September 2026 PDF is now
audited at Table 4, Table 5, and Appendix F/I level; the all-firm revenue
estimate is not statistically starred, employer-firm employment is about 2.25
workers in the paper's interpretation, and private-credit expansion remains a
new obligation as well as a recovery channel. The next step is to link this
firm-level result to worker pay/quality, customer access, owner-household
recovery, or local public capacity only where dates and identifiers permit.

The linked owner-household pass now supplies the adjacent household arrow:
business revenue fell 40% in the first two months of COVID-19, while each dollar
of lost revenue passed through as about 1.6 cents less owner consumption, with
the muted average response persisting through 2021. This is a different shock
and subsidy environment, so it is a cross-case bridge rather than a disaster-
loan effect. The next test is owner buffers, business survival, worker/customer
outcomes, and an aligned intervention/follow-up—not another aggregate
consumption cross-tab.

The Harvey customer-welfare case now extends the same chain to local access:
firm closures increased observed shopping distance and generated sharply
localized modeled welfare losses, while higher-value entry did not fully replace
stores in the hardest-hit neighborhoods. The next step is to align customer
income, vehicle access, trip purpose, and missed purchases with firm aid or
insurance receipt; the raw payment-card panel is not needed by default.

The Harvey recovery survey adds the judgment layer: 30% of affected residents
still reported disruption nearly a year later, 42% said they were not getting
needed help, and confidence that relief reached those most in need was lower
among more heavily affected groups. This is a descriptive legitimacy surface,
not a causal aid-to-action result; the next route is a lawful same-resident
link to verified aid, displacement, health/work recovery, and later civic
behavior.

**Higher-education aid usability rotation — 2026-09-22:** GAO reports that
9.9 million students were Pell-eligible in SY 2024–25, about 6% more than the
prior year, and maximum-award eligibility rose 31% after FAFSA simplification;
yet fewer students completed the FAFSA during the rollout. Gains were uneven,
and some household configurations could lose eligibility. This adds an
eligibility-to-application boundary; the next valid test is a protected
student route through submission, verification, award, disbursement,
enrollment, persistence, and exit. Do not treat eligibility as received aid or
college access. See the [Pell/FAFSA finding](projects/us-pell-fafsa-usability/findings/us-gao-pell-fafsa-eligibility-2026-001.md).

**School-participation rotation — 2026-09-22:** Department of Education data
count 13.4 million of 48.3 million students as chronically absent in 2022–23,
or 27.8%, with large state differences. This adds a participation boundary
between enrollment and usable school access. The next valid test is a protected
student or school episode joining absence reason, outreach, support,
transportation or housing context, learning, safety, belonging, and later
attendance or exit. Do not treat chronic absence as a single cause or as
permanent dropout. See the [attendance finding](projects/us-school-attendance-absence/findings/us-ed-chronic-absenteeism-2022-2023-001.md).

**Emergency-grant learning rotation — 2026-09-22:** GAO found that Education's
COVID-era Maintenance of Equity oversight used real-time guidance without
MOEquity-specific written procedures; unreliable data limited verification of
which districts were protected, and lessons were not reliably documented or
shared. This adds a crisis-action-to-institutional-memory boundary. The next
valid test is a later grant or emergency showing adopted procedures, verified
data, reused lessons, and school or student outcomes. Do not treat the rule,
funding, or recommendation as durable protection. See the [MOEquity finding](projects/us-education-grant-learning/findings/us-gao-k12-moequity-grant-learning-2026-001.md).

**Tribal-water maintenance rotation — 2026-09-22:** GAO found that IHS
property rules can exclude some homes from a project, multi-agency funding can
create high administrative costs, and Tribes remain responsible for operating
and maintaining systems after construction while routine IHS O&M funding is
generally unavailable. This adds a legal-eligibility and asset-maintenance
stage. The next valid test is a named system through connection eligibility,
construction, operator staffing, O&M spending, outage or service quality,
household reach, and later health or replacement cost. Do not treat a built
project or estimated need as durable safe water. See the [Tribal water finding](projects/us-tribal-water-infrastructure/findings/us-gao-tribal-water-infrastructure-maintenance-2026-001.md).

**Broadband deployment sustainability rotation — 2026-09-22:** GAO found that
all nine reviewed federal programs had begun distributing funds, but completed-
project data were available for only three; provider-reported maps and a
burdensome challenge process shape targeting, while BEAD projects extend to
2030 and beyond and sustainability monitoring remains incompletely specified.
The next valid test is a named location or project through map challenge,
award, construction, activation, operating finances, price, subscription,
reliability, and continuation. Do not treat an award, planned location, or
provider certification as durable digital access. See the [broadband
deployment finding](projects/us-broadband-deployment-sustainability/findings/us-gao-broadband-deployment-targeting-sustainability-2026-001.md).

**Wearable-health decision rotation — 2026-09-22:** GAO finds that wearables
could support faster, more personalized, and more remote care, while device
reliability, clinical workflow integration, privacy, liability, and unclear AI
autonomy remain open. This adds a data-to-care boundary. The next valid test is
a named program through device validation, data transfer, clinician response,
patient burden and privacy, treatment change, and later health outcome. Do not
treat sensor output or AI capability as improved care. See the [wearable-health
finding](projects/us-wearable-health-decision-making/findings/us-gao-wearable-clinical-decision-making-2026-001.md).

**Marketplace-broker consent rotation — 2026-09-22:** GAO found that federal
Marketplace broker licensing and registration did not reliably verify consumer
consent or notify consumers of all actions; confirmed complaints tied to
unauthorized enrollments and plan switches grew more than fourfold from 2023
to 2025, while at least 160,000 2024 applications had likely unauthorized
changes. Selected state Marketplaces use stronger controls such as one-time
passcodes. The next valid test is a protected plan-change ledger through
authorization, identity check, notice, correction, coverage continuity, and
care use. Do not treat registration or a complaint as a national prevalence or
lasting coverage-loss rate. See the [broker-consent finding](projects/us-marketplace-broker-consent/findings/us-gao-marketplace-broker-consent-2026-001.md).

**No Surprises provider-market rotation — 2026-09-22:** GAO found that
in-network claim shares increased after the No Surprises Act for three of four
selected specialties, while emergency payment trends largely continued paths
that began before the law. This adds a legal-protection-to-market-response
boundary. The next valid test is a protected claim and bill route through
network status, law applicability, negotiated payment, patient liability,
dispute, care continuity, and later financial outcome. Do not treat claim-share
change as lower patient cost or a clean causal estimate. See the [No Surprises
finding](projects/us-no-surprises-network-participation/findings/us-gao-no-surprises-network-participation-2026-001.md).

**Part D premium-stabilization rotation — 2026-09-22:** GAO reports that
without the 2025 demonstration average standalone-plan premiums would have
nearly doubled for continuing beneficiaries, while observed premiums rose only
from $42 to $43 and enrollment increased 2%. Medicare estimated $9.8 billion in
2025-2026 demonstration cost and took on more plan-sponsor risk. The next valid
test is a beneficiary-plan route through premium, subsidy, plan choice,
medication access, out-of-pocket spending, switching, and health or financial
outcome. Do not treat stable enrollment as medication access or a causal policy
effect. See the [Part D finding](projects/us-medicare-partd-premium-stabilization/findings/us-gao-medicare-partd-premium-stabilization-2026-001.md).

**Federal eligibility-data rotation — 2026-09-22:** GAO found data-quality
issues in all nine selected federal eligibility sources and cross-source
inconsistencies in seven; a partial match linked 2,074 awards to exclusion
records but did not establish improper payment, and no governmentwide
interoperability authority was designated. The next valid test is a protected
case ledger through identity, eligibility, award, exclusion review, correction,
repayment, and later outcome. Do not treat data matches as proof of wrongdoing
or claim a national error rate. See the [eligibility-data finding](projects/us-federal-eligibility-data-interoperability/findings/us-gao-federal-eligibility-data-interoperability-2026-001.md).

**Population insurance-coverage rotation — 2026-09-22:** CDC's preliminary
2025 NHIS estimates show exchange coverage rising from 4.3% of people under 65
in 2021 to 6.3% in 2025, while 28.0 million people remained uninsured and
adults ages 18-64 remained at 11.6% uninsured. The next valid test is a
protected person route through coverage transition, premium, cost-sharing,
network, delayed or received care, medical debt, and later health outcome. Do
not treat coverage status as affordable or usable care. See the [NHIS finding](projects/us-nhis-insurance-coverage-2025/findings/us-cdc-nhis-health-insurance-coverage-2025-001.md).

The [Harvey cross-source event ledger](projects/us-small-business-disaster-liquidity/data/harvey-firm-customer-resident-event-ledger-v1.json)
now preserves this chronology as four explicit arrows. It marks the firm,
customer/model, and resident survey units as non-pooled; the next decisive
artifact remains a lawful same-resident or same-firm remedy-and-outcome link.

The disaster-recovery synthesis now makes the cross-source architecture
explicit: public credit, owner cash buffers, customer travel, and resident
fairness judgments are separate currencies that can move in opposite
directions. The next broad pass should return to a different lane and seek a
same-unit event with verified remedy and action; no pooled resilience score is
licensed by the current evidence.

The small-business size-rule case adds an institutional-allocation counterpoint:
expanding support eligibility toward larger firms is associated with lower
revenue and more exits among the smallest firms, alongside lower wages and
patenting. It remains abstract-level evidence with customer prices, owner
households, and program-specific effect sizes open; the next step is a compact
threshold/table audit rather than a broad support-program aggregate.

### ILOSTAT comparison gate

ILOSTAT remains an open international comparison route for labor-force
participation, unemployment, working poverty, earnings, and youth exclusion.
The official catalog and bulk documentation are available, but the prior
candidate request returned zero bytes and the 2026-09-14 direct-route recheck
returned HTTP 404 HTML responses rather than CSV/GZIP data. No estimate is
promoted until the payload, indicator definition, source basis, reference area,
revision status, and matching US comparison are captured. See the
[ILOSTAT access audit](projects/ai-work-control/ilostat-access-audit-2026-09-15.md)
for the bulk and Rilostat API/RDS observations. The API metadata and RDS
routes also returned HTTP 200 with zero-byte `application/octet-stream`
responses; this is recorded as a delivery failure, not an empty dataset.
Its purpose is to
identify which missing variables prevent the existing evidence from becoming
an end-to-end societal result:

1. a dated bill, price, care need, rule, or work change;
2. the person or household's alternatives and schedule control;
3. the money and time response, including paid or unpaid substitution;
4. the protected and sacrificed outcomes; and
5. recovery, trust, collective action, or exit at a defined follow-up.

Until a same-unit or valid matched design supplies those fields, the safe
output is a measured distribution, an explicit comparison, or an acquisition
gap—not a claim that one cost caused one cultural or political outcome.

The [RECS household energy-burden layer](projects/us-household-calendar-integration/recs-energy-burden-household-layer-v1.md)
now supplies a same-household energy expenditure and assistance screen. The
next energy step is to connect this material vulnerability to dated bills,
housing tenure, health/care use, work or time substitution, and later trust or
political action; the 2020 RECS cross-section cannot establish those links.

The [LIHEAP reach/restoration record](records/us-liheap-reach-restoration-fy2024.json)
adds an official FY2024 public-capacity checkpoint: program reach and reported
home-energy restoration are separate endpoints, not a durable-stability rate.
The [LIHEAP performance-access recheck](projects/us-repeat-energy-crises/liheap-performance-access-recheck-2026-09-18.md)
now finds the official performance site accessible, with preliminary FY2025
state/grantee routes and restoration/prevention definitions visible. This
repairs the prior route-availability statement but does not create a
household-level panel: application, payment, reconnection, next-bill, and
repeat-crisis fields remain unobserved. The next stronger energy test is still
a same-household application, payment, restoration, next-bill, and repeat-use
ledger. A bounded API extraction now supplies national all-grantee occurrence
counts for FY2023–FY2025: post-disconnection restoration is 159,320, 166,991,
and 171,077; bill-payment prevention is 1,868,247, 1,752,072, and 1,853,734.
These values are preliminary and not unique-household rates; they improve the
program-performance layer without closing household recovery. See the
[machine-readable extraction](projects/us-repeat-energy-crises/data/us-liheap-performance-measures-2023-2025.json).
The same API also yields a selected-state FY2025 diagnostic for California,
New York, Ohio, Texas, and Virginia, pairing households served with reported
prevention and restoration occurrences. The derived occurrence-per-served-
household values expose large variation, but are explicitly not rates because
occurrences can repeat and the numerator/denominator units differ. See the
[selected-state diagnostic](projects/us-repeat-energy-crises/data/liheap-state-performance-diagnostic-fy2025.json).

The [MEPS Panel 27 health-cost longitudinal layer](projects/us-household-calendar-integration/meps-panel27-health-cost-longitudinal-layer-v1.md)
now supplies a repeated health-cost and coverage endpoint. The next material/
health step is to join valid panel health-cost change to care/time allocation,
employment, household resources, and treatment or work continuity, while
retaining the distinction between total expenditure, out-of-pocket spending,
coverage, and perceived health.
The [MEPS non-synchronization finding](projects/us-health-cost-household-choice/findings/us-health-cost-household-choice-001.md)
now records the interpretation and the counterexample: lower paired
out-of-pocket spending does not prove better health or lower total burden. The
next pass must add treatment continuity, unpaid care/time, employment, debt,
and food/housing trade-offs with design-based uncertainty.

The [2024 GSS financial-position and trust/politics layer](projects/us-cost-trust-politics/gss-2024-financial-position-trust-politics-layer-v1.md)
now supplies a same-respondent cross-sectional bridge from financial position to
trust, fairness, ideology, and vote intention. The next politics step is a
harmonized repeated-year or panel design with measured exposure and prior
identity, followed by direct action, institutional-response, and recovery
outcomes; this GSS layer is a co-occurrence screen only.
The [financial dissatisfaction/trust finding](projects/us-cost-trust-politics/findings/us-cost-trust-politics-012.md)
records the meaning boundary and counterexamples: distrust is not withdrawal,
and vote intention is not a measured response to a dated financial event. The
next pass must harmonize repeated years or use a timed panel with prior party
identity, attribution, civic action, and institutional response.

The [historical GSS financial/trust layer](projects/us-cost-trust-politics/gss-financial-trust-historical-layer-v1.md)
adds anchor-year context from 1972–2024. The next historical step is formal
harmonization of question availability, mode, weights, and covariate-adjusted
comparisons; the current layer deliberately avoids presenting the anchor years
as an unbroken causal trend. The new [historical GSS finding](projects/us-cost-trust-politics/findings/us-cost-trust-politics-024.md)
promotes that boundary into the reader-facing finding set: the within-year
financial-satisfaction/trust gradient recurs, while overall levels and gap size
move across decades. The next test remains harmonized repeated-year or timed
event evidence with prior identity, attribution, action, and recovery.

The new [household-room resource/tenure/liquidity finding](projects/us-household-calendar-integration/findings/us-household-calendar-integration-032.md)
keeps four adjacent but non-pooled surfaces visible: SIPP resource bands,
tenure-conditioned payment difficulty, SHED emergency-liquidity routes, and
consent-linked credit-balance change. It sharpens the material/time/care
extract specification by naming the missing middle—dated event, available
alternatives, payment or substitution choice, protected/sacrificed outcome,
and recovery—while preserving the PSID access gate as the next stronger test.

The [PSID 2023 field-audit finding](projects/us-household-calendar-integration/findings/us-household-calendar-integration-036.md)
now verifies the candidate backbone at the codebook level: the 2023 Family
File documents paid work, household labor, care, time pressure, health,
income, wealth, insurance, and utilities. The next pass is no longer field
discovery; it is the executed 2019/2021/2023 file audit with valid denominators,
weights, attrition, imputation handling, and first descriptive cells.

The new [SIPP utility/care/mortgage three-way diagnostic](projects/us-household-calendar-integration/sipp-utility-care-mortgage-three-way-diagnostic-v1.md)
places utility difficulty, annual child-care work prevention, tenure, and
December rent/mortgage hardship on the same identified person records. It
adds a joint-constraint screen and a useful no-utility-difficulty counter-
surface, but the care field is on an annual fall clock and the prevention
cells are sparse. The official 240-replicate rerun now supplies Fay-BRR
intervals, but it remains a diagnostic memo rather than a promoted trend
estimate. A separate `RFOODS` outcome layer now tests food security on the
same records without pooling it with mortgage hardship; its severity extension
shows 36.89% very-low food security in the joint utility-difficulty-plus-
assistance cell versus 4.40% with neither screen. This sharpens the
public-support/need boundary but does not close it; the next test is a dated
bill or assistance event.

The new [SIPP adjacent-month utility/care/outcome bridge](projects/us-household-calendar-integration/sipp-utility-care-following-outcomes-bridge-v1.md),
preserved as the [canonical renter-layer record](records/us-sipp-utility-care-following-outcomes-2024.json),
orders November utility difficulty and tenure beside December care-related
work prevention, mortgage hardship, and food insecurity. It matches 2,600
positive-weight pairs to all 240 replicates and therefore strengthens the
temporal screen, while preserving the warning that SIPP reference-period
fields may repeat across months. It remains descriptive; the next decisive
test is a dated bill, shutoff, payment-plan, or assistance event with follow-up.
The same bridge now adds upward, downward, and any income-to-poverty-band
movement as threshold outcomes. These are movement screens rather than dollar
recovery measures; the next test must observe the actual bill/resource event
and its later reversal or persistence.

The [SIPP childcare time-loss gate](projects/us-household-calendar-integration/sipp-utility-time-loss-following-gate-v1.md)
tests the more direct `ETIMELOST` endpoint conditional on `EWORKMORE=1`. Only
27 positive-weight November–December pairs survive the official universe and
all 27 match the replicate archive. This is a useful time-sacrifice boundary,
not a care-burden estimate; the next acquisition must observe both protected
and time-lost cases around a dated utility or provider event.
The broader resource-conditioned time-loss comparison is also preserved in the
[canonical time-loss record](records/us-sipp-childcare-time-loss-resource-2024.json).

The new [multi-clock material/time/care synthesis](projects/us-household-calendar-integration/findings/us-household-calendar-integration-033.md)
adds the end-to-end reader frame: SIPP monthly resource/work transitions,
MEPS annual health-cost and health-status transitions, and SHED/ATUS care and
time surfaces are complementary clocks. The next acquisition remains a
same-person or same-family design that observes the dated trigger, alternative,
time/care substitution, protected or sacrificed outcome, recovery, and later
meaning/action without pooling incompatible samples.

The new [MEPS expenditure-conditioned finding](projects/us-health-cost-household-choice/findings/us-health-cost-household-choice-002.md)
adds a same-panel conditioning test: baseline total health-expenditure bands
have different perceived-health and employment-continuity profiles. Because
spending is also a marker of health need, age, retirement, insurance, and
service mix, the next acquisition must add treatment continuity, out-of-pocket
burden, unpaid care/time, debt, and baseline employment rather than promote a
health-cost causal effect.

The new [CMS-to-MEPS household health-cost synthesis](projects/us-health-cost-household-choice/cms-meps-household-health-cost-end-to-end-synthesis-v1.md)
places CMS national spending, payer and sponsor architecture beside MEPS
person-level expenditure, coverage, health, work, income, and utilization
transitions. It closes a presentation and interpretation gap between system
scale and household evidence without claiming a same-bill care decision,
medical-debt episode, unpaid-care substitution, trust response, or political
action. The next acquisition remains an event-oriented same-household route
with a dated need or bill, care decision, substitution, recovery, and
institutional response.

**Cohesion-as-national-resilience rotation — 2026-09-26:** the UK *Protecting
What Matters* Command Paper links economic insecurity, public-space decline,
technology, migration, extremism, online echo chambers, foreign influence, and
institutional trust, then proposes confident, cohesive, and resilient-community
pillars. This adds a state-diagnosis-to-policy-delivery-to-security route, not
independent causal evidence. The next valid test joins Pride in Place,
integration, platform controls, local services, social-contract experience,
belonging, trust, participation, safety, and resistance to hostile influence.

**Neighbourhood belonging-and-trust rotation — 2026-09-26:** England's
2025/26 Community and Engagement Survey reports 61% strong neighbourhood
belonging, 69% monthly neighbour chat, 61% perceived collective pull-together,
38% local trust, and 79% agreement that different backgrounds get along. It
also shows large local-authority and deprivation gradients and 31% saying their
area worsened over two years. This adds an official place-to-belonging-to-trust
route, not respondent-level linkage or causal community evidence. The next
valid test joins local assets and services to housing, safety, mobility,
cultural participation, trust, collective action, and exit or political action.

The new [public-system route-to-judgment synthesis](projects/us-safety-net-access/findings/us-safety-net-access-014.md)
rotates the program into the public-systems lane. It places administrative
timeliness, recipient-reported notice/time barriers, SIPP following hardship,
and Gallup institution-specific confidence into one bounded architecture. The
next acquisition remains a same-case episode record with notice, effort,
decision, amount/timing, interruption, remedy, material result, judgment, and
action; the WBNS respondent-file gate remains open.

The new [CFPB route-vintage audit](projects/us-customer-automation-recourse/findings/us-customer-automation-recourse-021.md)
rotates depth into consumer power. It tests the live API's two clocks—timely
label versus derived receipt-to-company-send lag—and audits the disappearance
of the narrative field in the current response surface. The next acquisition
must hold field definitions constant and add account exposure, effort, verified
correction, repeat contact, switching, and exit.

The new [USAspending supplier-concentration finding](projects/ai-work-control/findings/ai-work-control-072.md)
rotates depth into infrastructure/geopolitical capacity. It turns the
JASSM/LRASM recipient count into a concentration and repeat-recipient test,
showing why supplier-name breadth is not replaceability. The next pass must
link recipient names to parents, facilities, milestones, output, acceptance,
and substitute qualification before calling the network resilient or leveraged.

The new [official entity-parent-facility reconciliation finding](projects/ai-work-control/findings/ai-work-control-076.md)
adds the next bounded identity step. DLA CAGE records resolve the BAE route
from the reported Merrimack recipient through BAE Systems, Inc. to BAE Systems
plc, and resolve General Dynamics-OTS facilities through General Dynamics
Corp. The hierarchy sharpens jurisdiction and facility questions, but does not
assign the JASSM/LRASM work to a plant or establish workforce, production,
acceptance, delivery, replaceability, or leverage. The next pass must join
exact CAGE/UEI identifiers to procurement transactions and then trace facility
assignment, output, acceptance, and alternatives.

The follow-up [recipient-identifier ambiguity audit](projects/ai-work-control/findings/ai-work-control-077.md)
tests that join rather than assuming it. USAspending's official recipient
endpoint returns 17 BAE rows across 10 UEIs and three General Dynamics-OTS
rows, while the retained subaward rows contain no UEI/CAGE. One General
Dynamics UEI overlaps the selected DLA facility set, but this is not proof of
the selected subaward's plant assignment. The next acquisition must obtain an
identifier-bearing award/subaward or performance record and preserve endpoint
denominators, identifier vintage, component, production, acceptance, and
delivery fields separately.

The richer [subaward-to-UEI and location finding](projects/ai-work-control/findings/ai-work-control-078.md)
advances that gate. An official award-search route exposes a subrecipient UEI,
recipient location, and primary performance place for all 74 rows. The BAE
selected row resolves to `V7X9P6J9SUK1` in Nashua, NH; the General
Dynamics-OTS row resolves to `KZK8C85C1T94` in Niceville, FL. This closes the
recipient-identity/reporting-location link, not the CAGE-to-plant,
production-to-acceptance, delivery, or replaceability links. The next pass
must reconcile those UEIs to facilities and performance records without
collapsing reported location into manufacturing site.

The [facility-capability context finding](projects/ai-work-control/findings/ai-work-control-079.md)
adds independent capability evidence at both reported locations. BAE's
official certificate names 95 Canal Street, Nashua within a military-electronics
production/servicing scope; General Dynamics-OTS material names Niceville
Operations and warhead capability. The next pass must still obtain a
site-specific work-package, production, acceptance, delivery, or audit record;
capability context is not a JASSM/LRASM production assignment.

An official USAspending comparator now shows the same General Dynamics-OTS UEI
and Niceville address on a separate Army M1128 ammunition award whose public
description reaches manufacture, test, packaging, and delivery and whose
transaction history contains later modifications. This validates a promising
entity/facility route, but it is not evidence for the JASSM/LRASM subaward. The
next pass must keep the focal Lots 22–26 row separate and seek a work-package,
